{{group-theory-stub}}

In [[group theory]], especially, in [[geometric group theory]], the class of free-by-cyclic groups have been deeply studied as important examples. A [[group (mathematics)|group]] <math>G</math> is said to be '''free-by-cyclic''' if it has a [[free group|free]] [[normal subgroup]] <math> F</math> such that the [[quotient group]] <math> G/F</math> is [[cyclic group|cyclic]]. In other words, <math>G</math> is free-by-cyclic if it can be expressed as a [[group extension]] of a free group by a cyclic group (NB there are two conventions for 'by'). Usually, we assume <math> F </math> is finitely generated and the quotient is an infinite cyclic group. Equivalently, we can define a free-by-cyclic group constructively: if <math> \varphi </math> is an automorphism of <math> F </math>, the semidirect product <math> F \rtimes_\varphi \mathbb{Z} </math> is a free-by-cyclic group.

An isomorphism class of a free-by-cyclic group is determined by an [[Out(Fn)|outer automorphism]]. If two automorphisms <math> \varphi, \psi </math> represent the same outer automorphism, that is, <math> \varphi = \psi\iota </math> for some [[inner automorphism]] <math> \iota </math>, the free-by-cyclic groups <math> F \rtimes_\varphi \mathbb{Z} </math> and <math> F \rtimes_\psi \mathbb{Z} </math> are isomorphic.

==Examples and results==
The study of free-by-cyclic groups is strongly related to that of the attaching outer automorphism. Among the motivating questions are those concerning their non-positive curvature properties, such as being [[CAT(0) group|CAT(0)]].
* A free-by-cyclic group is [[hyperbolic group|hyperbolic]], if and only if it does not contain a subgroup isomorphic to <math>\mathbb{Z}^2</math>, if and only if no nontrivial [[conjugacy class]] is left invariant by the attaching automorphism (irreducible case: Bestvina and Feighn, 1992; general case: Brinkmann, 2000).<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Brinkmann |first=P. |date=2000-12-01 |title=Hyperbolic automorphisms of free groups |url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/PL00001647 |journal=Geometric and Functional Analysis |language=en |volume=10 |issue=5 |pages=1071–1089 |doi=10.1007/PL00001647 |issn=1420-8970|arxiv=math/9906008 }}</ref>

* Hyperbolic free-by-cyclic groups are [[Fundamental group|fundamental groups]] of compact non-positively curved [[Cubical complex|cube complexes]] (Hagen and Wise, 2015).<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Hagen |first1=Mark F. |last2=Wise |first2=Daniel T. |date=2015-02-01 |title=Cubulating hyperbolic free-by-cyclic groups: the general case |url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00039-015-0314-y |journal=Geometric and Functional Analysis |language=en |volume=25 |issue=1 |pages=134–179 |doi=10.1007/s00039-015-0314-y |issn=1420-8970|arxiv=1406.3292 }}</ref>

* Some free-by-cyclic groups are [[relatively hyperbolic group|hyperbolic relative]] to [[Free abelian group|free-abelian]] subgroups. More generally, all free-by-cyclic groups are hyperbolic relative to a collection of subgroups that are free-by-cyclic for an automorphism of polynomial growth.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Ghosh |first=Pritam |date=2023 |title=Relative hyperbolicity of free-by-cyclic extensions |url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/compositio-mathematica/article/relative-hyperbolicity-of-freebycyclic-extensions/B5F9111E9EBE0CE289D7B115CF61C2A0 |journal=Compositio Mathematica |language=en |volume=159 |issue=1 |pages=153–183 |doi=10.1112/S0010437X22007813 |issn=0010-437X|arxiv=1802.08570 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Dahmani |first1=François |last2=Li |first2=Ruoyu |date=2022 |title=Relative hyperbolicity for automorphisms of free products and free groups |url=https://www.worldscientific.com/doi/10.1142/S1793525321500011 |journal=Journal of Topology and Analysis |language=en |volume=14 |issue=1 |pages=55–92 |doi=10.1142/S1793525321500011 |issn=1793-5253|arxiv=1901.06760 }}</ref>

* Any [[Finitely generated group|finitely generated]] subgroup of a free-by-cyclic group is [[Finitely presented group|finitely presented]] (Feighn and Handel, 1999).<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Feighn |first1=Mark |last2=Handel |first2=Michael |date=1999 |title=Mapping Tori of Free Group Automorphisms are Coherent |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/121081 |journal=Annals of Mathematics |volume=149 |issue=3 |pages=1061–1077 |doi=10.2307/121081 |jstor=121081 |issn=0003-486X|arxiv=math/9905209 }}</ref>

* The [[conjugacy problem]] for free-by-cyclic groups is solved (Bogopolski, Martino, Maslakova and Ventura, 2006).<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Bogopolski |first1=O. |last2=Martino |first2=A. |last3=Maslakova |first3=O. |last4=Ventura |first4=E. |date=2006 |title=The conjugacy problem is solvable in free-by-cyclic groups |url=http://doi.wiley.com/10.1112/S0024609306018674 |journal=Bulletin of the London Mathematical Society |language=en |volume=38 |issue=5 |pages=787–794 |doi=10.1112/S0024609306018674 |issn=0024-6093|url-access=subscription }}</ref> (Bridson and Groves 2010) <ref name=BridsonGroves>{{Cite journal |last1=Bridson |first1=Martin |last2=Groves |first2=Daniel |date=2010 |title=The quadratic isoperimetric inequality for mapping tori of free group automorphisms |url=http://www.ams.org/books/memo/0955/ |access-date=2024-11-02 |journal=Memoirs of the American Mathematical Society |volume=203 |issue=955 |doi=10.1090/S0065-9266-09-00578-X |language=en|arxiv=math/0610332 }}</ref>

* Free-by-cyclic groups are conjugacy separable (Dahmani, Hughes, Kudlinska, and Touikan 2026)<ref>{{cite arXiv |last1=Dahmani |first1=F. |last2=Hughes |first2=S. |last3=Kudlinska |first3=M. |last4=Touikan |first4=N. |date=2026 |title=Free-by-cyclic groups are conjugacy separable |arxiv=2509.22346 |class=Math.GR}}</ref>

* Notably, there are non-CAT(0) free-by-cyclic groups (Gersten, 1994).<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Gersten |first=S. M. |date=1994 |title=The automorphism group of a free group is not a CAT(0) group |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/2161207 |journal=Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society |volume=121 |issue=4 |pages=999–1002 |doi=10.2307/2161207 |jstor=2161207 |issn=0002-9939|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

* However, all free-by-cyclic groups satisfy a quadratic [[isoperimetric inequality]] (Bridson and Groves, 2010)<ref name="BridsonGroves" />.

* All free-by-cyclic groups where the underlying free group has [[Rank of a group|rank]] <math>2</math> are CAT(0) (Brady, 1995).<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Brady |first=Thomas |date=1995-05-26 |title=Complexes of nonpositive curvature for extensions of F2 by Z |url=https://dx.doi.org/10.1016/0166-8641%2894%2900072-B |journal=Topology and Its Applications |volume=63 |issue=3 |pages=267–275 |doi=10.1016/0166-8641(94)00072-B |issn=0166-8641|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

* Many examples of free-by-cyclic groups with polynomially-growing attaching maps are known to be CAT(0).<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Samuelson |first=Peter |date=2006-09-01 |title=On CAT(0) structures for free-by-cyclic groups |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0166864105003214 |journal=Topology and Its Applications |volume=153 |issue=15 |pages=2823–2833 |doi=10.1016/j.topol.2005.12.002 |issn=0166-8641|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Lyman |first=Rylee Alanza |date=2023 |title=Some New CAT(0) Free-by-Cyclic Groups |url=https://projecteuclid.org/journals/michigan-mathematical-journal/volume-73/issue-3/Some-New-CAT0-Free-by-Cyclic-Groups/10.1307/mmj/20205989.short |journal=Michigan Mathematical Journal |volume=73 |issue=3 |pages=621–630 |doi=10.1307/mmj/20205989 |issn=0026-2285|arxiv=1909.03097 }}</ref>

* Free-by-cyclic groups are [[Equationally noetherian group|equationally noetherian]] and have [[Well-order|well-ordered]] [[Growth rate (group theory)|growth rates]] (Kudlinska and Valiunas, 2025).<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Kudlinska | first1=Monika | last2=Valiunas | first2=Motiejus | title=Free-by-cyclic groups are equationally Noetherian | date=2025 |volume=392 |pages=525–546 |journal=[[Mathematische Annalen]] |doi=10.1007/s00208-025-03096-8|doi-access=free }}</ref>
